title: Halve It, Tenth It
intro: You own the 10% machine. Today we bolt on more gears.

blocks.html:
Your gears so far:

10% — divide by 10.
5% — halve the 10%.
1% — divide the 10% by 10.
20% — double the 10%.

Quick warm-up before the new gears.

blocks.hint: 10%: slide the digits — 140 → 14. Then halve for 5%.

blocks.html:
25% is a quarter.

To find a quarter: halve it, then halve it again.

25% of £80: half is £40, half again is £20.

No percent machine needed — just two halvings.

50% is a half. One halving. Done.

75% is three quarters. Find the quarter, then times it by 3.
75% of £40: quarter is £10, so 75% is £30.

blocks.prompt: Build strange percentages out of your gears — like Lego:
Boss question — the SALE. A £36 jacket is 25% off. (This one was on your diagnostic. You have the gears now.)
blocks.hint: First find 25% of £36 — halve it, halve it again. Then take that off the price.

blocks.html:
📈 Market story for the dinner table: why is everything priced £9.99 instead of £10?

One penny can't matter to the shop… so why do they all do it? Work out what a customer's brain sees first, then ask Dad if it works on him. (Be honest: does it work on you?)

done.title: Meeting adjourned ✓
done.html:
10, 5, 1, 20, 25, 50, 75 — and combinations. You can now build nearly any percentage in your head, which is more than most adults in the shop can do.
